# V2.0.0-beta - Radian

This is a **pre-release for beta testers**. Install it only if you agreed to test it. Installed stable copies are not offered this build by the in-app update check; the stable release stays 1.1.1 until 2.0.0 is final.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Back up `~/.pi` before you install a beta over an existing installation. To leave the beta, uninstall it and install the stable release again.

Since 1.1.0: 38 commits, 695 changed files, about 71,700 added lines. This is the largest change to Fate UI so far. The 1.1.1 hotfix (saved sessions larger than 128 MiB) is part of this build.

## The short version

- Fate no longer has to run on the computer you sit at. A **Node companion** can own the project and the model credentials, and you work on it from a **browser** or from the **desktop app over SSH**.
- The desktop app moves to **Pi SDK 1.0** (from 0.85.1) and gains an **MCP client**, **questions from the agent** and a **Monitor dashboard**.
- Ownership and recovery were rebuilt around one rule: **after a crash or a lost connection, nothing is run again without you**.
- An optional **native durable storage** (SQLite) with a reviewed migration path. The default storage is unchanged.

## New: run Fate away from the desktop

### Node companion (`fate-server`)

A plain Node process that owns Pi, your registered workspaces and the provider credentials. No Electron, no window. Closing a client does not stop it.

- `fate-server init` creates a private profile for a trusted workspace. `fate-server serve` runs it headless; `fate-server web` also serves a login page.
- `fate-server provider login` and `provider status` set up the model provider on the host itself. Keys never go through a browser.
- `fate-server doctor` reports the state of a profile without changing it.
- `fate-server auth-code` issues a one-use browser login code. `fate-server access-key create` issues a workspace-scoped client credential for a desktop.
- Profiles created this way start with a **read-only maximum permission, the terminal off and browser integration off**. The permission maximum and the terminal are raised only by explicit flags at `init`.
- The host listens on `127.0.0.1` only. There is no public mode and no mode without login.
- A guide for a Linux user service: `docs/v2/remote-host-service.md`.

### Browser workspace

Sign in with the one-use code, pick a registered workspace, and work in it:

- Chat, model selection, sessions and the message queue.
- GoalMax, tasks and Agent Team controls.
- The Monitor view.
- File tree and text preview of the registered root; text can be attached as context.
- Git status, diff and history.
- Saved conversation history, read page by page from the start.
- Permission changes, down and up, each confirmed by a one-use transaction. Nothing above the host's maximum is granted.
- An optional manual terminal in the browser, when the host was set up for it.

### Desktop app to a remote host over SSH

Add an SSH profile in the desktop host selector, then select it or run `fate connect PROFILE`. The app opens the tunnel through your system OpenSSH, checks the host identity, the protocol and the workspace, and then works on the remote project. An unknown or changed host key blocks the connection. A failed connection never starts a local agent as a fallback.

### Several clients, one controller

- A client starts as an **observer**. It must claim control before it changes anything. Control is a lease that the host owns; it does not raise the permission.
- When control moves to another client, requests from the earlier one are refused.
- The selected session is shared in a workspace: when the controller selects another session, every client follows.
- If the answer to a command is lost, the client reviews that same command afterwards. It does not send it again.
- After a reconnect or a host restart, the client needs a fresh snapshot before it can control again. Interrupted work is shown as interrupted, not resumed.

### What the network client does not do yet

- No built-in browser, file reveal, voice, hotkeys or rich media over the network.
- No commit, revert, fetch, pull or push from a network client.
- No terminal in the desktop-over-SSH client; the network terminal is browser only.
- No provider-key or MCP editing from a browser; that stays on the host.
- Saved Agents, Routines and Memory Learning are local-desktop only.
- No separate selected session for each client.

The full table is in `docs/v2/current-status.md`.

## New in the desktop app

- **Pi SDK 1.0.** A prompt is either admitted by Pi or refused; there is no half-queued item. The color format of Pi 1.0 themes is supported.
- **MCP client.** Settings → MCP: add a local command or an HTTPS endpoint, test it, and turn it on. No server is on by default, and no project file can start one. The agent can use MCP tools only in a Full access session.
- **Questions from the agent.** Pi can stop and ask you one or more questions, each with two to four choices and a field for your own answer. You answer in a card in the conversation.
- **Monitor dashboard.** One panel lists the runs, Teams, tasks and activity that are active or need attention. The agent can read the same dashboard with a tool; it cannot approve, stop or resume work through it.
- **Agent Teams.** A sub-agent that works in an isolated worktree now keeps its own sub-agents in that worktree, unless it asks for another workspace. After a restart, a saved Team is checked against its stored child sessions, and nothing is run again.
- **Large saved sessions.** A session file is read as a stream with a bounded preview in memory. Sessions and Agent home sessions larger than 128 MiB open, and the file is never shortened.
- **`fate` command.** New: `fate connect PROFILE`. The launcher also passes `init`, `serve`, `web`, `provider`, `auth-code`, `access-key` and `doctor` to an installed companion.
- **Push-to-talk** runs its keyboard hook in a helper process. A hook that hangs can no longer freeze the app; push-to-talk is then reported as unavailable.
- **One owner for each profile.** A second app or host on the same data is refused, so two processes cannot write the same state. After a crash, a forced quit or a power loss, the next start recovers the lock when the old process is gone.

## Storage and recovery

- The default storage is unchanged (`legacy-json`). Existing sessions, Team history and worktrees are kept as they are.
- **Native durable storage** (`native-durable`, SQLite through Pi's durable runtime) is opt-in for a new profile. It holds the queue, the tasks and the GoalMax documents.
- **Migration** of existing state is a separate procedure on the host: `fate-server migrate` shows a dry run, then `prepare`, `apply` with a verified private backup, and `rollback` (`docs/v2/migration-cli.md`). It does not copy provider credentials, trust or full-access grants, and it does not replay old work.
- **Workflow review.** After an uncertain stop, native workflow history must be reviewed before new work is admitted (`docs/v2/native-workflow-review.md`).
- A storage close that could not be confirmed keeps the profile locked for an operator. An ordinary crash does not.
- A wrong, corrupt or incomplete native store blocks the start. It never falls back to the old storage silently.

## Security defaults

- Browser login uses a one-use code with a five-minute life, exchanged in a POST body, then an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict session cookie and a CSRF token. Requests with a wrong Host or Origin are refused.
- Profile and credential files must be private. Windows ACLs and POSIX modes are checked, and a profile that is not private is refused.
- Workspaces must be registered and trusted on the host. A remote path never leaves the host.
- The manual terminal is an unsandboxed shell of the host account. It needs an explicit acknowledgement flag at `init`, current control, and a warning confirmation in the browser.
- Full access stays an explicit, unsandboxed grant.

## Fixed since 1.1

- The application could fail to quit: every quit started the global keyboard hook only to stop it, and that start could block for good.
- The music player reported a missing yt-dlp when the bundled one needed more than five seconds to start.
- The Git view could receive a status that was read before the agent's latest edit.
- A tooltip covered neighboring controls after a dialog returned focus to its opener. Tooltips now open from keyboard focus only.
- The Activity panel showed ledger rows for one frame after a project lost trust.
- Narrow inspector tabs, panel splitters, focus outlines on search fields, select filters after a keyboard choice, and the Monaco fallback workers.

## Found by the first V2 package runs, fixed before this beta

- The installers lacked 165 runtime libraries.
- The two standard Pi themes were missing on a profile without its own Pi themes.
- The browser terminal lost its connection and its control when a shell ended.
- The Windows `fate` launcher failed on a PC with several Node installations, and under the default Windows script policy.

## Please test and report

- Starting again after a forced quit or a crash.
- Push-to-talk (Settings, voice hotkey in push-to-talk mode), especially on macOS and Linux: no automated check can press a global hotkey.
- Agent Teams with isolated worktrees and nested sub-agents.
- MCP servers you use, and questions asked by the agent.
- A Node companion with a browser, and the desktop app over SSH.

## Known limits

- The **Node companion is not among these release files.** Its builder supports Linux x64 only; build it from this tag with the steps in `build/server-package/README.md`. It needs Node 22.19 or later.
- On Windows and macOS a lock left by a crash stays while another program holds the old process number; it is recovered once that program ends.
- Lock recovery needs a filesystem with hard links.
- `--new-instance` still shares one profile owner: a second instance on the same profile is refused.
- Real SSH hosts, a Linux service installation and push-to-talk in the packaged macOS and Linux apps were not exercised by an automated runner.
- Installers remain unsigned, and macOS builds are not notarized. Verify downloads with `SHA256SUMS`.

## Install and trust

The artifact set is Windows x64 EXE; macOS Apple Silicon and Intel DMG and PKG; Linux x64 AppImage and DEB; plus `SHA256SUMS`. This build passed the package, install and smoke matrix on all four runners, and the exact seven-installer checksum set was verified before publishing.
